text: Aldabra tortoises wallow in mud, which helps protect them from mosquitoes.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Smithsonian National Zoo, Aldabra tortoise fact sheet; https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/aldabra-tortoise. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Boreal chorus frogs in Yellowstone tolerate freezing while dormant in leaf litter or beneath woody debris during winter.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: National Park Service, Yellowstone amphibians; https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/nature/amphibians.htm. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Columbia spotted frogs overwinter in water that does not freeze, while local salamanders and toads use underground refuges.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: National Park Service, Yellowstone amphibians; https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/nature/amphibians.htm. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Plains spadefoots spend much of the year underground. Their spadelike feet help dig the burrows used for shelter and overwintering.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: National Park Service, Yellowstone amphibians; https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/nature/amphibians.htm. Consulted 2026-10-13.
